reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, full StructureDefinition report, selected R4/R6 package StructureDefinitions, the direct HTTP behavior finding, shared behavior findings as context only, and R4 maturity. I formed the resource-level conclusion from the actual replacement/remodeling shape before comparing it with the deterministic aggregate.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` is trial-use/FMM 0, so the compatibility burden is weak compared with mature or normative resources. That low maturity means most structural breaks are not automatically standards-review problems, but it does not erase regulatory, IDMP, substance-identity, strength, confidentiality, or resource-identity risk where migration can be lossy or production-relevant.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` is replaced by R6 `Ingredient` and substantially remodeled, so a migration program is unavoidable; routine element-shape breaks become local migration work, but identity transition and specified-substance fidelity still deserve standards attention.

reasoning.thesisMd: This is not a mostly stable same-resource evolution. The R6 package has `Ingredient`, no same-name `MedicinalProductIngredient` StructureDefinition, and `fhir-old-types` lists `MedicinalProductIngredient` as an old resource name. Existing instances fail first at `resourceType`/canonical identity and then require substantive transforms for status, manufacturer, substance identity, specified-substance content, and strengths. Low R4 maturity weakens the presumption against change, but the resource still represents medication/product ingredient data with credible regulatory and safety relevance.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a resource replacement plus model remodel: create R6 `Ingredient`, choose a required modifier `status`, wrap each manufacturer reference in a manufacturer backbone, convert coded substances into `CodeableReference.concept` or references to `SubstanceDefinition`, decide whether R4 `specifiedSubstance` entries split into multiple R6 Ingredients or collapse into one, preserve or map specified-substance group/confidentiality, convert strength fields to R6 choice names such as Ratio/RatioRange/Quantity/text variants, backfill required reference-strength substances, and decide allergen placement when a `SubstanceDefinition` reference is used.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The resource identity break really does lower the leverage of preserving ordinary child-element wire shapes: an untouched R4 JSON instance remains invalid as R6 even if some old paths were retained. For planning, the migration program dominates. That is not the same as saying additional break prevention has no value. The highest-value compatibility work is at transition seams that can avoid broad remapping or data loss: retaining/deprecating the old resource identity or endpoint alias, publishing a precise cross-version map, and preserving specified-substance group/confidentiality semantics. By contrast, status backfill, manufacturer wrapping, CodeableReference conversion, and strength choice serialization are mainly migration chores once the R6 Ingredient redesign is accepted.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest less-breaking alternative is resource identity preservation: R6 could plausibly have kept `MedicinalProductIngredient` as the base resource name while evolving the model, or provided a deprecated compatibility resource/endpoint alias. A second standards-review-worthy alternative is retaining deprecated `specifiedSubstance` content or adding explicit R6 fields for its group, confidentiality, and repetition semantics. Other alternatives are only partial: making `status` optional would weaken lifecycle guarantees; retaining direct manufacturer references alongside role backbones would create duplicate association forms; keeping old Ratio/low-limit strength fields beside R6 choice/range fields would create safety-sensitive consistency problems.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: The direct HTTP behavior finding says the base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints, including `MedicinalProductIngredient`. For this resource that is derivative of the same replacement decision: generic clients, route discovery, conformance tests, and endpoint matrices must move to `Ingredient` or a server-specific compatibility alias. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings such as `$meta`, `$validate`, and shared search metadata can affect generic clients operating on Ingredient/MedicinalProductIngredient data, but they are context only for this resource-level structure judgment.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The independent conclusion agrees with the deterministic aggregate on the headline labels: major migration is already unavoidable, the migration shape is a removed/replaced resource, and resource-level planning is dominated by a migration program. The important nuance is that this agreement is not count-driven and should not be read as dismissing local standards concerns. The resource identity finding and the lossy `specifiedSubstance` collapse remain high-value preservation/review targets even though most other hard breaks become local tasks inside the broader migration.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the computable structure differences and endpoint-discoverability issue. Confidence is lower for the exact intended business mapping because the supplied inputs did not include an official `MedicinalProductIngredient` to `Ingredient` ConceptMap, rendered ballot rationale, terminology-server expansions, or an instance corpus showing how often specified substances, confidentiality, low limits, and missing reference substances occur.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 MedicinalProductIngredient is absent in R6 and appears replaced by Ingredient
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the decisive migration-program signal. `resourceType`, canonical URL, parser dispatch, generated classes, and REST type identity all change before any child-element mapping can help. Even with FMM 0, the same high-level definition and old-type marker make an identity-preserving transition or deprecated alias a plausible standards-review item.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 Ingredient adds required modifier `status` with required publication-status binding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Every migrated record needs a lifecycle status selected from policy or source governance, and clients must honor the modifier meaning. The break is proportionate after accepting the R6 definitional-resource model because lifecycle status prevents retired or draft ingredient definitions from being treated as active.

findingConsiderations.title: `manufacturer` changes from direct Organization Reference to a backbone with manufacturer role
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a real serializer/codegen break, but it is a localized shape transform: move each Organization reference under `manufacturer.manufacturer` and optionally populate manufacturer role. Preserving both direct references and role-bearing association backbones would create synchronization and interpretation risks.

findingConsiderations.title: `substance` becomes mandatory and its code changes from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Substance identity is central to the resource, and R6 makes it mandatory while changing the representation to CodeableReference. This drives the model-remodel conclusion because records that relied on `specifiedSubstance` or simple CodeableConcept JSON need classification and possibly SubstanceDefinition policy, not just a property rename.

findingConsiderations.title: R4 `specifiedSubstance` branch is removed/collapsed, with unclear handling for repeated specified substances and confidentiality
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most important child-level standards concern. It can require expert decisions about splitting or merging resources and can lose group/confidentiality semantics in a regulatory/disclosure-sensitive area. The broader migration program does not make this harmless; explicit R6 fields, a deprecated branch, or authoritative mapping guidance would materially reduce risk.

findingConsiderations.title: Strength presentation and concentration fields become choice elements and low-limit fields are removed
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Strength conversion is safety-sensitive and must be tested carefully, especially low-limit-to-RatioRange handling. It is nevertheless mostly a migration chore after the R6 redesign is accepted because the choice/range/text model has a credible rationale and retaining old and new quantitative encodings side by side could create contradictory strengths.

findingConsiderations.title: `referenceStrength.substance` becomes required and reference-strength values use choice serialization
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 reference strengths lacking a substance need backfill or rejection, and strength values need choice-property conversion. The required substance is clinically reasonable because reference strength without the referenced substance is ambiguous, so this is high-risk migration work rather than a strong argument to preserve the R4 base shape.

findingConsiderations.title: New `ing-1` invariant constrains allergen use with SubstanceDefinition references
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is only a potential forward break: direct CodeableConcept-to-CodeableReference.concept migration can avoid it. It matters for enriched migrations that reference `SubstanceDefinition` while retaining `allergenicIndicator`, but the single-source allergen rule is safety-rational and belongs in migration policy.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds optional fields with no clear R4 representation
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Optional R6 additions such as product linkage, function, comment, text strengths, basis, and repeatable identifiers do not make R4-origin instances invalid. They are R6-to-R4 loss/round-trip concerns, not evidence that the R4-to-R6 migration is broader than the replacement/remodel already shows.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 adds several terminology bindings that change conformance expectations
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The main retained coded fields use example bindings, so legacy codes are not rejected by this finding alone. Required bindings attach to new or separately remodeled fields such as `status` and manufacturer role, so terminology is not an independent resource-level compatibility driver.

findingConsiderations.title: The full base CapabilityStatement no longer advertises many R4 resource REST endpoints
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Because `MedicinalProductIngredient` is among the removed advertised endpoints, generic clients and conformance tooling will not discover the old REST type in the R6 base CapabilityStatement. This reinforces the resource-identity migration and supports considering endpoint aliases or explicit replacement metadata, but it is derivative of the resource lifecycle decision rather than a separate data-model break.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Generic clients managing metadata on ingredient records may see this shared Resource operation change, and the behavior-level preservation concern is real. It is not specific to `MedicinalProductIngredient`, so it does not alter the resource-level migration-shape classification.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Validation clients migrating ingredient data can be affected by the shared `$validate` invocation semantics, but this belongs to the Resource/operation behavior review. It should be handled alongside generic validation migration, not counted as local Ingredient model remodeling.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared search-parameter metadata can affect generated clients or conformance tests that also operate on ingredient resources. It is shared Resource/DomainResource infrastructure context and does not drive the `MedicinalProductIngredient` resource-level conclusion.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit or explicitly document the `MedicinalProductIngredient` to `Ingredient` identity transition. Prefer retaining the old resource identity if still possible; otherwise publish authoritative endpoint/canonical/resourceType replacement metadata and cross-version maps so generic clients and validators do not infer the mapping ad hoc.

Resolve `specifiedSubstance` migration at standards level, including repeated specified substances, group, confidentiality, and whether data should split into multiple R6 `Ingredient` resources, map to explicit R6 fields, or use a deprecated compatibility branch/extension.

Publish implementer migration guidance and test cases for required `status`, manufacturer backbone wrapping and role, CodeableReference/SubstanceDefinition choices, allergen placement under `ing-1`, and Ratio/RatioRange strength conversion.
Define R6-to-R4 loss policy for R6-only fields such as `for`, `function`, comments, text strengths, basis, non-Ratio strengths, multiple identifiers, and SubstanceDefinition references.

caveats: No official `MedicinalProductIngredient` to `Ingredient` ConceptMap or ballot rationale was available in the supplied inputs, so some mapping intent is inferred from StructureDefinitions and old-type markers.
No representative instance corpus was reviewed, so prevalence of specified substances, confidentiality, strength low limits, missing status, and missing reference-strength substance is unknown.
Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were treated as context only, as required, because the reviewed resource is neither `Resource` nor `DomainResource`.
